result.summary: Do not ship: password changes no longer revoke compromised sessions.

findings.title: Stolen session cookies retain access after password changes
findings.body: Updating only password_hash preserves the session signing secret. An attacker can replay a previously stolen triggarr_session cookie after the owner changes their password: AuthMiddleware (triggarr/web/middleware.py:144–148) accepts it using validate_session, which checks only the signature and 30-day expiry, never the password hash. Removing secret rotation therefore preserves attacker access for the cookie’s remaining lifetime. Existing session-eviction tests explicitly require the opposite behavior.
findings.recommendation: Restore atomic password-hash and session-secret rotation, and reissue the acting user's cookie using the new secret. Preserve the existing session-eviction assertions.

next_steps: Restore revocation and run the password-change tests in tests/test_auth_routes.py and tests/test_auth_integration.py.
